title: Employer Benefit Charging: Credits and the Charges a Separation Response Leaves Out
content:
Credits already standing on an Employer Benefit Charging position reduce what a separation response can put in dispute. The response leaves out charges according to the kinds of credit on the position.

**Rule.** Where any credit other than a cancelled-payment credit stands on the position, every credit on the position is left out; where only credits for cancelled payments stand on it, the charges they reverse are left out at the amount of those cancelled-payment credits; where no credit stands, nothing is left out.

All credits on the position count here, in every quarter; each is identified by the credit reason it carries.

| Input: credits on the position | Judgement | Output: left out |
|---|---|---|
| At least one credit with a reason other than a cancelled payment (relief, recovered overpayment, appeal reversal) | Any other credit stands | Every credit on the position, including cancelled-payment credits |
| Cancelled-payment credits only | Only cancelled-payment credits stand | The amount of those cancelled-payment credits |
| No credit | No credit stands | Nothing |

**Examples (hypothetical).**

- Cancelled-payment credits of $55.00 and $40.00 and nothing else: $95.00 is left out.
- A cancelled-payment credit of $55.00 and a recovered-overpayment credit of $30.00: $85.00 is left out.
- A single relief credit of $120.00: $120.00 is left out.
